summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — PTC +33%, VST +15%, NRG +12%, CEG +12%, ILMN +8%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (CHRW -11%, LEN -7%, CAT -6%, CRWD -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: PTC (+33.49%) — Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC for $205/share in cash (~$22.6B, 42% premium to the $144.03 prior close). The +33.49% close-to-close move matches that jump. Sources dated it Oct 5, not Oct 8. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: PTC is a mid/large-cap US industrial software name that no strategy lists. The gap was a pre-market M&A jump, and the stock then pinned below the $205 offer. Momentum and news filters see no tradable follow-through.

top_movers.catalyst: Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC for $205/share in cash (~$22.6B, 42% premium to the $144.03 prior close). The +33.49% close-to-close move matches that jump. Sources dated it Oct 5, not Oct 8.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: PTC is a mid/large-cap US industrial software name that no strategy lists. The gap was a pre-market M&A jump, and the stock then pinned below the $205 offer. Momentum and news filters see no tradable follow-through.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an M&A-target detector (news keywords like 'to acquire'/'definitive agreement' plus a gap ≥ +25%) that auto-adds the ticker to the news-reactive universe. Cap it at merger-arb sizing and skip chasing the gap.

top_movers.catalyst: No Oct 8 article found. Likely continued IPP/nuclear rally: Oct 6 Google–Constellation 890 MW deal and DOE's $4.2B conditional loan for Vistra nuclear uprates, with VST up ~10% that day.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: VST is a ~$55B+ independent power producer (utilities/IPP), not in the universe of any strategy. The move followed a multi-day news-driven run, so a gap or RSI filter would also likely have blocked a late entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a utilities/IPP and AI-power basket (VST, CEG, TLN, NRG) to the momentum universe, with an entry rule on a sector-peer gap of ≥ +8% on ≥2.5× average volume. A ~$55B cap would pass the liquidity floor.

top_movers.catalyst: No Oct 8 headline found; likely continuation of the Oct 6 rebound: independent power producers (CEG, VST) rallying on AI data-center power demand, plus renewed activist pressure at NRG, after a ~35% YTD drawdown.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: NRG is a mid/large-cap independent power producer (utilities/IPP) that no strategy covers. It was also a sector-wide rebound with no single-name earnings or M&A event, so news-reactive filters had nothing to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an IPP/power-demand basket (NRG, VST, CEG, TLN) to the momentum universe, entering when the sector is up 2+ days in a row with volume ≥1.5× the 20-day average, so a sector move catches laggards too.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely continued nuclear/IPP rally from Google's 20-year, 890 MW reactor-uprate deal with Constellation (announced Oct 6). I couldn't confirm a separate Oct 8 trigger, and press prices for Oct 6 don't line up cleanly with today's close.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CEG is a large-cap utility/IPP, likely excluded by sector or defensive-utility screens. The news-driven jump started two days earlier, so any gap or volume trigger had already fired or been missed by Oct 8.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'power_ai_nuclear' basket (CEG, VST, TLN, OKLO, LEU) to the news-reactive universe, and let it enter on a sympathy move of at least +5% in a peer within 2 sessions of a hyperscaler power-deal headline.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-10-08. Searches turned up no same-day Illumina news. The stock has run from ~$190 in July to $293, so this looks like momentum or sector-driven (genomics/tools).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ILMN is a mid-cap life-science tools name that no strategy's universe includes. With no pre-market news trigger, a news-reactive bot had nothing to key on, and a +7.6% close-to-close move with no catalyst would only show up after the fact.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a dynamic universe-expansion rule so any Nasdaq/NYSE name above ~$10B market cap with a ≥+5% close and ≥1.5× 20-day average volume is added to the momentum-trader watchlist for the next session.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely tied to CRL's 2026 Investor Day: >$300M cumulative savings (2027-30), 5-7% organic growth target, 2026 results at upper end of guidance. Search could not confirm the date matches today's +7.09%.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CRL is a mid-cap life-sciences/CRO name that no strategy covers. The move was also a scheduled-event gap, which a post-open momentum signal would see too late.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap healthcare/CRO names such as CRL to the momentum universe, and add an event-day entry rule for ≥+5% gaps on ≥1.5× average volume within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely the Oct 5 announcement that CHRW will buy RXO for $5.8B (57% cash, 43% stock, ~$3B new debt, buybacks paused). I found no distinct Oct 8 news, so today's -10.85% may be a stale or multi-day move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid-cap transport/logistics broker). The move was also M&A-driven, so the gap came at the Oct 5 open and the bot's post-gap signals came too late. The long-only bot also can't short an acquirer sell-off.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an M&A-acquirer watch rule: when a universe-adjacent name gaps ≤-8% on deal news, flag it for a mean-reversion long only after 2 stabilising closes. Also add mid-cap transports like CHRW to the mean-reversion universe.

top_movers.catalyst: No same-day news found for LEN on 2026-10-08. A -6.7% drop with no company-specific event fits a homebuilder sector selloff, likely from rising Treasury yields or mortgage rates. This is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: LEN is a mid/large-cap homebuilder (consumer-cyclical, rate-sensitive) that no strategy includes. A sector-wide, non-earnings drop also gives a momentum or news-reactive bot no single-name trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a rate-sensitive sector basket (LEN, DHI, PHM, TOL, or the XHB ETF) to the mean-reversion universe, gated on a ≥5% one-day drop with ≥1.5× average volume. Otherwise treat this as a no-op, since we can't short.

top_movers.catalyst: Truist cut its CAT price target from $1,225 to $1,100 (Buy kept), citing doubts about AI/data-center power-generation spending, high rates and rising diesel costs. CAT is about 30% below its peak.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CAT is a very large-cap industrial (~$800+/share) that none of the strategies include. The drop was an analyst-driven AI-capex derating, which a long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot would not buy into. Dip-buying also looks unattractive with CAT near its 200-day EMA.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mega-cap AI-infrastructure industrials (CAT, GEV, FTAI) to the mean-reversion universe, gated to enter only after price holds above the 200-day EMA. Alternatively, use a cluster-selloff flag to skip these names.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-10-08; searches turned up no CRWD-specific story, so this looks like a sector-wide cybersecurity/software selloff or technical move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CRWD is a large-cap cybersecurity software name that none of the strategies list. With no news catalyst, a -4.7% drift would also not trigger a news-reactive entry, and a long-only bot gains nothing from a loser.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap software/cybersecurity names (CRWD, PANW, ZS) to the mean-reversion universe, with an entry gate of a sector-wide drop of 4% or more on no stock-specific news, so the next sector flush is tradable.
